name: Romano-Wolf Stepdown Multi-Rule Book
note: Ten candidate rules run side by side and NONE of them is allowed to trade until it survives a family-wise-error-controlled test. Every rerun bars, each rule's per-bar return over the trailing win bars is studentised with a Newey-West HAC standard error, and B stationary bootstrap paths - the SAME index paths shared across all ten rules, so the procedure exploits how correlated near-duplicate rules are instead of being crushed by them - build the null of the max studentised statistic. Rules above the (1-alpha) quantile are rejected as genuine, removed from the active set, and the null is REBUILT over what is left, so the critical value falls and the second and third best rules get a fair hearing. Only the rejected set votes; the book is the equally-weighted net of their positions, and with an empty rejected set the book is flat and stays flat until a later rerun finds something. The k-FWER variant (kfwer > 1 uses the k-th largest bootstrap statistic) is the power-for-false-positives trade the idea lists.
source: Romano, J. P. & Wolf, M. (2005), 'Stepwise Multiple Testing as Formalized Data Snooping', Econometrica 73(4), 1237-1282. Also Romano, J. P., Shaikh, A. & Wolf, M. (2008), 'Formalized Data Snooping Based on Generalized Error Rates', Econometric Theory 24(2), 404-447 (k-FWER and FDP-controlling variants that let you tolerate a few false positives in exchange for far more power).
